title: Junior Data Analyst
description: Junior Data Analyst, Commercial Insights. We are looking for a junior analyst to turn our sales, customer and marketing data into reliable reports and answers for the business. Responsibilities: write SQL queries that pick out the right records from the warehouse, narrow them down with conditions, remove duplicates and present results in a useful order; combine customer, order and product tables, including customers who have not ordered yet; summarise revenue and volumes with counts, sums and averages per region, month or segment, keeping only groups that pass a threshold; treat missing or unknown values carefully so blank discounts or regions do not silently distort totals or comparisons; break complicated questions into step-by-step queries built from nested queries and named intermediate results; calculate running totals, month-over-month changes and rankings within each group. In Python you will clean, merge, group and reshape data with pandas DataFrames, write small reusable functions with sensible parameters and return values, and use lists, dictionaries and sets with concise one-line transformations and lazily evaluated pipelines that stream through large files row by row. You will tidy text fields such as names, product codes and comments by splitting, slicing and normalising them, and keep scripts fast as data grows by using dictionary or set lookups instead of repeatedly scanning lists and by reasoning about how running time scales with the number of rows. Requirements: working SQL and Python with pandas, and clear communication with non-technical colleagues.

title: Junior Backend Engineer
description: Junior Backend Engineer, Platform Team. Join the team that builds the Python services behind our booking platform's web API. Responsibilities: design and implement API endpoints and business logic in Python, organised into well-structured classes with clear responsibilities, inheritance where it helps, and small functions with clear arguments, return values and variable scope; avoid subtle bugs caused by shared state, such as an object being changed unexpectedly through another reference, and pick the right built-in containers (lists, tuples, dictionaries, sets) for each job; validate input and handle failures deliberately by raising, catching and logging errors so that resources are always cleaned up; build request handlers and background workers that run concurrently with threads and asyncio, understanding the limits of Python's global interpreter lock; design relational tables with primary and foreign keys, uniqueness rules and sensible normalisation, and write queries that combine data from related tables; diagnose slow queries by reading execution plans and adding the right indexes; keep bookings consistent when several requests update the same rows at once, using transactions with the appropriate isolation level. You will also choose efficient in-memory structures and reason about their time and memory cost as traffic grows: hash-based caches and lookups, job queues and undo stacks, the doubly linked list behind a least-recently-used cache, and ordered tree-based structures for range lookups. Requirements: solid Python fundamentals, working knowledge of relational databases, and curiosity about how systems behave under load.

title: Junior Data Engineer
description: Junior Data Engineer, Data Platform. You will help build and operate the batch pipelines that move data from our product databases and event logs into the analytics warehouse. Responsibilities: write Python ETL jobs as small, reusable, well-tested functions, using lists, dictionaries and sets, and stream records through lazy generator pipelines so that multi-gigabyte files never have to fit in memory; clean, merge and reshape extracts with pandas before loading; make jobs robust by catching and handling bad records and failed connections and failing loudly with clear error messages instead of silently losing data; write advanced SQL: joins across many tables, grouped aggregations, multi-step logic with common table expressions and correlated subqueries, and window functions for deduplication, running totals and the latest record per key; design warehouse tables with proper primary keys, foreign keys and constraints; keep loads and queries fast by adding indexes and reading query plans; load data atomically inside transactions so a failed run never leaves tables half-updated, and choose the isolation level that controls what other sessions can see while a load is running. You will also reason about the time and memory cost of your code as volumes grow: join and deduplicate in memory with hash maps, sort large extracts and merge already-sorted files, locate records quickly with binary search, keep the top N results with a heap-based priority structure, and run jobs in the right order by traversing the pipeline's dependency graph. Requirements: strong SQL and solid Python.
